issues.legal_issue: A revenue authority exercising revisional power over permission to use land for building purposes must do so within a reasonable time, even if no fixed time limit is prescribed.
material_facts: Permission was granted to use agricultural land for non-agricultural building purposes.
The Commissioner set aside the Collector’s permission more than a year after it was granted.
The Court observed that an occupant is likely to spend money on building operations within a few months after permission is granted.
issues.conclusion: The Commissioner acted too late, and the revisional order was properly quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Reading sections 65 and 211 of the Bombay Land Revenue Code, 1879 together, the Court held that revisional power must be exercised within a reasonable time. What is reasonable depends on the circumstances and the nature of the order; for permission to build, the likely commencement of expenditure makes a period of a few months appropriate. No earlier case was relied on for this holding.

predicates.revision_of_land_use_permission: A revenue authority reviewed an order granting permission to change the use of land.
predicates.permission_for_building_use: The permission allowed the land to be used for building purposes.
predicates.revision_after_reasonable_time: The reviewing authority acted only after a delay that was unreasonable in the circumstances, considering the likely consequences of the permission.

issues.definition: When a revenue authority reviews permission to change land use for building after an unreasonable delay, its revisional order is invalid for that delay.

issues.legal_issue: A revenue authority setting aside an administrative order must give reasons for its conclusions.
material_facts: The Commissioner set aside the Collector’s permission after reciting the Municipality’s objections and the arguments made on the occupant’s behalf.
The Commissioner stated his conclusions, including that the land did not belong to the occupant, without explaining the reasons for those conclusions.
issues.conclusion: The Commissioner’s order was properly quashed because it did not give reasons.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that a decision of this kind must indicate its reasons, however briefly, so that an aggrieved party can decide whether to pursue the matter further. The Court relied on no specific statutory provision or earlier case for this holding.

predicates.revenue_revision_proceeding: A revenue authority exercised revisional power over an administrative order.
predicates.decision_sets_aside_administrative_order: The reviewing authority set aside the order under review.
predicates.decision_gives_conclusions_without_reaso: The reviewing authority stated its conclusions without explaining the reasons supporting them.

issues.definition: In a revenue revision, setting aside an administrative order without explaining the reasons makes the decision invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A revenue authority should not decide a serious dispute about an occupant’s title to land and should instead refer the parties to a competent court.
material_facts: The Municipality disputed the occupant’s title to the land before the Commissioner.
The Commissioner concluded that the land did not belong to the occupant.
The dispute about title was serious.
issues.conclusion: The Commissioner erred by deciding the title dispute; the appropriate course was to refer the parties to a competent court.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that when a party raises a serious dispute about an occupant’s title before the Collector or Commissioner, the revenue authority should refer the parties to a competent court rather than decide title itself. This holding was made in the context of sections 65 and 211 of the Bombay Land Revenue Code, 1879; no earlier case was relied on for it.

predicates.revenue_permission_proceeding: A revenue authority considered a proceeding concerning permission to use land for a different purpose.
predicates.serious_title_dispute: A party raised a serious dispute about the occupant’s title to the land.
predicates.revenue_authority_decides_title: The revenue authority decided the disputed question of title itself.

issues.definition: When a serious title dispute arises in a land-use permission proceeding and the revenue authority decides it, the authority has acted improperly and the parties should be referred to a competent court.
